html_source: Molly’s feelings about sex are untraditional for the time, but she is unapologetic in her admittance of it. Although she is aggravated when thinking of Leopold’s past affairs, she values the idea of sexual freedom all the same. This is similar to the emphasis on female autonomy in D.H. Lawrence’s Lady Chatterley’s Lover; both exemplify the introduction of more radical sexual perspectives in early twentieth-century literature.
